task.description: Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's ISS-0692 design amendment (step-02-code-designer.json). Verify §1.5's coverage of both ISS-0692 acceptance criteria, cross-references, §7 AC map update, soundness of the redaction/accepted-risk rejection reasoning, correctness of the AC2 implementation-trigger judgment call, absence of implementation code, no scope creep, and independently confirm whether test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/ exists on this branch (bearing on whether a retroactive-compliance gap exists).
acceptance_criteria: Design amendment covers both ISS-0692 ACs
New §1.5 is unambiguous and binding, not hedged
§2.2/§4.1 cross-references present and correctly worded as preconditions
Reasoning for rejecting redaction and accepted-risk is sound, including verification of the §3.4 unconditional-pixel-diff claim and the swiftroute scenario spot-check
AC2's conditional (code required only 'if chosen') correctly applied to the policy-only choice
No implementation code present; visual-baseline.ts change is comment-only
Independent confirmation of whether test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/ exists on this branch

result.summary:
Read lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md directly (current HEAD content, not CODE-DESIGNER's summary), the ISS-0692 issue record, the ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis, CODE-DESIGNER's handoff, the swiftroute scenario fixture, and the actual `web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts` diff. Most of the design amendment is sound (see below), but one of this gate's required independent checks fails outright, and it undermines a load-bearing factual claim both ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis and CODE-DESIGNER's own re-verification made. Per WF-02 Step 1b, a single failed check fails the gate completely -- no partial credit.

CHECKS THAT PASS:
1. §1.5 ('Data-sensitivity policy for baseline content (binding, not an open question)') exists, states the synthetic/disclosed-fictional-data-only invariant as a decision ('Decision, stated as an invariant of this mechanism'), not a suggestion or hedge. Covers ISS-0692 AC1 directly.
2. §2.2 and §4.1 each carry an explicit 'Precondition (§1.5)' paragraph before their numbered steps/role description, correctly worded as a precondition on calling accept/rebaseline, matching the task's requirement.
3. §7's AC map gained the exact new row claimed: '(data-handling scope implicit in AC-1/AC-2...) | §1.5 (...)'.
4. §8's four open questions (OQ-1..OQ-4) were left untouched -- confirmed by reading the full section; no new open question was added, matching the explicit instruction to resolve this as a stated decision.
5. Reasoning for rejecting redaction is sound and independently verified against §3.4's actual text: §3.4 does state 'once a baseline exists ... any pixel difference Playwright's comparison detects ... fails that expected outcome immediately and mechanically. No agent ... is consulted to decide whether the detected diff counts' -- this is genuinely an unconditional mechanical diff, so a redaction mask's bit-for-bit-stability requirement genuinely conflicts with it, exactly as §1.5 argues.
6. The swiftroute spot-check is accurate: `test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/swiftroute/tenant-onboarding-happy.yaml`'s header comment states 'Ported verbatim from R-Co ... disclosed-synthetic fixtures', and its actor is Alice Bauer / alice.bauer@swiftroute.example / swiftroute.bpm.example -- matches §1.5's characterization exactly.
7. No implementation code was added. `git diff 35d3489a..HEAD -- web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts` shows only two JSDoc comment-block additions (above `acceptBaseline` and `rebaseline`) -- verified line-by-line; `acceptBaseline`/`rebaseline`'s function bodies are byte-for-byte unchanged in the diff.
8. No scope creep: the diff touches only the design doc's new §1.5 plus the §2.2/§4.1/§7 cross-references, and the two comment-only additions to visual-baseline.ts -- nothing else in the affected_files list, nothing beyond ISS-0692's fix direction.
9. AC2's conditional judgment (code required only 'if a redaction or synthetic-data mechanism is chosen') is, on its own terms, a defensible reading: a content/authoring-discipline policy genuinely is not something acceptBaseline/rebaseline's code can mechanically verify from PNG bytes, so choosing that policy over a redaction transform does not by itself trigger AC2's implementation clause. I do not disagree with this half of the judgment call.

CHECK THAT FAILS -- independent confirmation of `test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/`:
Both ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis ('zero PNGs exist under test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/ today') and CODE-DESIGNER's own re-verification (explicitly listed as this run's acceptance criterion #1, 'Prior diagnosis re-verified against current file state ... before editing') assert this directory does not exist on this branch, and CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary states outright: 'Confirmed test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/ still does not exist anywhere in the tree ... so the diagnosis's premise (design-only fix, no retroactive baseline to fix) still holds.' This is FALSE. `git ls-files test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines` on this branch returns four tracked files: `platform/req362-visual-regression-selfcheck/01-EO-001.local.png`, its `.yaml` sidecar, and two `_disputed/ISS-0691/` PNGs -- landed in commit 242ae72c ('REQ-362: two-phase visual regression testing ... (#1460)'), confirmed an ancestor of this branch's HEAD (merged to main before this ISS-0692 branch's base 35d3489a). The sidecar's own content (`accepted_by: ELIXIR-DEV`, `accepted_in_run: WF02-REQ362-20260916`, `judgment_detail`: 'Root route (GET /) ... for an unauthenticated session, the real Keycloak login form') confirms this baseline is REQ-362's own self-check against an unauthenticated screen -- consistent with ISS-0692's own description that REQ-362 itself never touches a real authenticated screen, and I could find no PII in it. So SUBSTANTIVELY there is no retroactive redaction/PII exposure in the actually-committed baseline, and no re-baseline (§4) or accept (§2) call site has yet processed a screen with real tenant data.

WHY THIS STILL FAILS THE GATE, not just a nitpick: two independent agents in this run's chain (ISSUE-FIXER, then CODE-DESIGNER explicitly re-verifying against 'current file state ... before editing' as its own stated acceptance criterion) both asserted a checkable fact that is false and easily falsified by `git ls-files`/`find`. This is exactly the class HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §1.1 exists to catch ('a handoff's factual premises are checkable, and may be wrong ... verify it before building on it'), and it means the design's §1.5 enforcement-note reasoning ('no code change is required ... no baseline has yet been committed for the policy to apply retroactively to' -- paraphrased from the diagnosis this design inherits) rests on a false premise, even though the conclusion happens to still be correct once the actual baseline's content is checked. A design amendment whose own stated verification step is factually wrong is not a reliable artefact to build on, under humanless operation: nothing downstream will catch this unless it is caught here.

issues.description: CODE-DESIGNER's handoff (step-02-code-designer.json) and the ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis it inherited both falsely assert `test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/` does not exist on this branch. It does: `git ls-files test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines` returns 4 tracked files from commit 242ae72c (REQ-362's own merged implementation, an ancestor of this branch). The design's §1.5 must be corrected to state the true premise: a baseline already exists (REQ-362's own self-check, an unauthenticated screen with no tenant PII per its sidecar's judgment_detail), so the invariant is compliant today by inspection, not because nothing has been committed yet. Re-verify this specific claim with `git ls-files test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines` (not a working-tree `find`/`test -d` alone) before restating it.

Once §1.5's premise is corrected, consider whether the design should also state explicitly that the existing self-check baseline was independently spot-checked and found compliant (unauthenticated Keycloak login screen, no tenant data at all) -- this closes the loop ISS-0692 raised rather than leaving a reader to wonder whether the one baseline that does exist was ever checked against the new policy.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER (rework iteration 1 of 3): correct §1.5's factual premise per the MAJOR issue above -- state plainly that `test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/` already contains a committed baseline (REQ-362's own self-check, landed via #1460), verified compliant with the new policy because it captures only an unauthenticated Keycloak login screen with no tenant data. Do not reintroduce this as an open question in §8; state it as a verified fact alongside the existing decision. Once corrected, re-dispatch to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for re-gate before routing to Step 3 (SECURITY-REVIEWER then REVIEWER).
